content_metadata.description: The video explains the concept of electromotive force (EMF) in galvanic cells, detailing how electrode potential differences drive electron flow and generate EMF.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The video is relevant for audiences interested in understanding basic concepts in electrochemistry, specifically focusing on how electromotive force (EMF) is generated in galvanic cells.

narrativeProgression.description: The man begins explaining that a galvanic cell is made up of two half cells.
The man writes the explanation on a whiteboard.
The man explains that one electrode must have higher value of electrode potential and the other must have lower value.
The man explains that electrons move from higher to lower electrode potential.
The man explains what electromotive force is.
The man writes the mathematical formula for calculating electromotive force.
The man explains the mathematical formula for calculating electromotive force.
The man explains how the oxidation potential of the overall cell depends on the oxidation potentials of individual halves.
